# Artifact freshness, persist/commit policy, and governance

Scope: proposals 13, 14, 17; open questions Q-002, Q-006, Q-010.

## Sources read

- `/private/tmp/.../research/00-context.md` — shared track context — confirmed
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/wisp/docs/04-decisions-and-open-questions.md` — Q-002, Q-006, Q-010 — confirmed
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/wisp/docs/03-delivery-plan.md` — Milestone 0/1/2 gates — confirmed
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/wisp/docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md` lines 51-66, 140-178 — dependency table and persist receipt — confirmed
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/agent-plugins/shared/constitution.md` — Spec/Plan Persistence, Spec Staleness Detection, Schema-Driven Handoffs — confirmed
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/agent-plugins/shared/schemas/spec@1.json`, `plan@1.json` — confirmed
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs` lines 100-170, 320-380 — `commits_since_with_pathspec` — confirmed
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/permit.rs` lines 32-46 — `ApplyPermit` — confirmed
- `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/{callisto-vcs,callisto-model,callisto-graph}/Cargo.toml` — per-crate licenses — confirmed
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12329 — PROJECTMEM abstract — confirmed
- https://arxiv.org/html/2606.12329v1 — PROJECTMEM full text — confirmed
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/riponcm/projectmem/main/README.md (801 lines, read locally) — staleness rule, `--supersedes`, commit/gitignore split, precheck — confirmed
- https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/spec-driven.md — Spec Kit artifact chain — confirmed
- https://tessl.io/registry/spec-driven-development/spec-as-source/3.0.0 — `targets` ownership, `[@test]`, three check scripts — confirmed
- https://martinfowler.com/articles/exploring-gen-ai/sdd-3-tools.html — Kiro/spec-kit/Tessl comparison — confirmed
- https://kiro.dev/docs/specs/ (via search snippets; `/docs/specs/concepts/` 404s) — "Sync Files" is manual — likely
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adr/madr/main/template/adr-template.md — MADR status field — confirmed
- log4brains superseded-by link handling (GitHub discussion #22, issue #35, via search) — likely
- https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/descriptor-format/ — relations derived from typed spec fields — confirmed
- https://docs.rs/gix/latest/gix/struct.Repository.html — `rev_walk`, `status`, `is_dirty`, `diff_tree_to_tree` — confirmed
- https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/descriptor.md — digest grammar and registered algorithms — confirmed
- https://json-schema.org/blog/posts/custom-annotations-will-continue — `x-` keywords collected as annotations — likely
- https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/issues/662 + docs/concepts.md (via search) — capability id = relative path — likely
- cargo-release dry-run writes files without committing (crate-ci/cargo-release issue #872, via search) — likely
- Changesets `commit` config option (docs/command-line-options.md) — confirmed but page self-marked outdated
- kubectl apply `unchanged` vs `configured`; Ansible `ok` vs `changed` (via search) — likely

## Findings

1. **PROJECTMEM's staleness rule is commit-distance over a decision's cited file, and it is advisory-with-human-adjudication, not blocking.** README: "Every decision that cites a file is cross-checked against that file's git history — when the file has moved on, the memory is *flagged* ("predates 7 commits to auth.py — confirm or supersede") and a human decides." The rendered precheck output shows the payload shape Wisp needs: subject path, a count, and the citing artifact's id — `decision [evt_9db5a3f8…] "auth uses session cookies, 30min timeout" — predates 7 commits`. There is no threshold constant in the README or paper; any N ≥ 1 flags. Source: README lines 296, 711-720.

2. **The paper and the README disagree about what the mechanism is, and the README is the authoritative one for the staleness feature.** The paper's related-work section distinguishes PROJECTMEM from "Codified Context", whose "drift detector fires at *session start* from git-commit divergence, not from the project's logged failures and not *per action*", and describes PROJECTMEM's own gate as `precheck_file(path)` consulting the event log for failed attempts, open issues, and high churn — a path lookup, not a distance computation. The README documents both: `precheck` (event-log lookup) *and* stale-memory detection (commit distance, new in 0.1.4) as separate features surfaced in the same warning block. Treat them as two mechanisms, not one. **Consequence for Wisp: commit distance answers "is this evidence still trustworthy", and it is a different question from "has this artifact's own bytes changed".** Conflating them is the main modelling hazard here.

3. **PROJECTMEM never deletes and never mutates: staleness is a flag, retirement is `--supersedes`, and the superseded event stays in the append-only log tagged forever.** `pjm decision "new way" --supersedes <id>`; MCP tool `add_decision(summary, supersedes?)`. Comparison table rows: "Stale memory: **flag, never delete**" and "Supersede without losing history", both marked unique versus 12 contemporary systems, which "silently decay or delete", "down-rank and prune via decay", "rewrite facts on update", or "self-edit in place".

4. **PROJECTMEM's commit/gitignore split is: distilled outputs committed, raw log and runtime state gitignored.** Committed: `summary.md`, `PROJECT_MAP.md`, `AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md`, `issues/`, and `plan` ("It's committed (not gitignored) so intent is shared with your team"). Gitignored: `events.jsonl`, `watch.pid`, `watch.log`, and `structure.json` — the last described as "derived from code, gitignored, and never committed — code is only ever *read*." This is exactly Wisp's D-001/D-007 split (canonical artifacts committed, `.wisp/` derived cache gitignored) arrived at independently.

5. **Silence is audited.** `pjm precheck --snooze 2h` "silences it politely — the snooze is itself logged, so even the silence is audited", and "every commit shows one dim line so silence is never mistaken for a clean check." This is the governing principle for Q-002's degradation path: a declined commit must be a recorded state, not an absent one.

6. **No spec-driven tool in the survey detects staleness between its own artifacts by hash or link.** Spec Kit: `/speckit.plan` reads the spec, `/speckit.tasks` reads `plan.md` — no hash, no freshness marker, no version tracking; the doc's "Living Documentation" claim is a conceptual goal, not an implemented safeguard. Kiro: tasks carry requirement numbers (`1.1, 1.2, 1.3`), and re-sync is an explicit user action ("Sync Files", "Refine") — the tool does not notice on its own that `requirements.md` moved ahead of `tasks.md`. Martin Fowler's three-tool comparison contains no mention of hash-based versioning or drift detection for any of the three. **Wisp's `plan@1.spec_hash` mechanism is ahead of all three.**

7. **Tessl's spec-as-source is the only one enforcing spec↔code linkage mechanically, and it does so by link integrity and ownership, not hashing.** Frontmatter `targets` declares the files a capability spec owns; requirements carry `**Verified by**: [@test] tests/path/test_file.py`. Three scripts enforce it: `check-spec-links.sh` (every `[@test]` resolves to an existing file), `check-target-ownership.sh` (a target file cannot change without its spec changing), `build-spec-manifest.py` (spec → requirements → targets → tests map). Semantic drift — "code does something the spec doesn't describe (or vice versa), despite links and tests being formally in place" — is explicitly left to an agent review, not automated. Two lessons: the manifest is built, not hardcoded; and the ownership check is *exactly* commit-distance over declared paths, which is Wisp proposal 13.

8. **ADR tooling has a status lifecycle and a supersession pointer, but no code linkage and no drift detection at all.** MADR frontmatter: `status` ("proposed", "rejected", "accepted", "deprecated", or "superseded by ADR-0123"), `date` ("when the decision was last updated"), plus `decision-makers`/`consulted`/`informed`. Supersession is encoded *inside the status string*, not as a separate typed field — log4brains inherits this and requires the link text to be the target ADR's slug exactly, which its own maintainers call "too restrictive". "An ADR is immutable — only its status can change." **Do not copy the status-string encoding**; Wisp should carry `superseded_by` as its own typed field. PROJECTMEM's `--supersedes` (finding 3) is the better model because it is a first-class argument.

9. **Backstage derives relations from typed schema fields rather than declaring edges in code — direct precedent for proposal 17.** "Entity descriptor YAML files are not supposed to contain this field. Instead, catalog processors analyze the entity descriptor data and its surroundings, and deduce relations." `spec.owner` → `ownedBy`, `spec.dependsOn` → `dependsOn`, `spec.providesApis` → `providesApi`, `spec.system` → `partOf`, each auto-reversed (`dependencyOf`). These are schema properties, not annotations, and the processor is generic. Backstage exposes `metadata.etag` for change detection but has no last-updated staleness banner or CI freshness check for entities or TechDocs.

10. **Callisto already implements the exact git primitive Wisp needs, and its git crate is permissively licensed.** `callisto-vcs` and `callisto-model` are `MIT OR Apache-2.0`; only `callisto-graph` and the repo root LICENSE are AGPL-3.0-only. So `GitDataSource::commits_since(&self, since_ref: Option<&str>, pathspecs: &[PathBuf]) -> Result<Vec<GitCommit>, VcsError>` and its gix implementation `commits_since_with_pathspec(since: Option<&CommitSha>, pathspecs: &[PathBuf])` are reusable as code, not merely as a design pattern. **This materially narrows Q-003.**

11. **The bounded-walk technique in that implementation is the reason it is cheap enough to run per artifact-link.** It uses `repo.rev_walk(vec![head.id]).with_hidden(Some(since_oid))` — gix's hidden-tip frontier algorithm, "exactly the same 'boundary commit' algorithm `git rev-list branch ^tag` itself uses" — instead of a second unbounded walk collected into an exclusion set, so "the walk stops once every in-flight branch has been resolved instead of continuing to the repository's first commit." Pathspecs "match as directory/path prefixes against a commit's tree diff vs. its first parent — mirrors `git log -- <pathspecs>`'s scoping, not full git pathspec magic"; merges are skipped. The crate instruments `REVWALK_VISIT_COUNT`, i.e. the authors treat walk cost as a measured budget.

12. **gix exposes everything the freshness enum needs, at workspace granularity.** `Repository::rev_walk(spec) -> Result<RevWalk<'static>, Error>`, `status(options) -> Result<Status, Error>`, `index_worktree_status`, `tree_index_status`, `is_dirty() -> Result<bool, Error>`, `head_commit`, `head_tree_id`, `diff_tree_to_tree(old, new, options) -> Result<Vec<ChangeDetached>, Error>`. Note `is_dirty()` returns only a bool — the *set* of dirty paths, which `Freshness::DirtyAffected` requires, needs `status`/`index_worktree_status`.

13. **OCI's digest grammar registers both SHA-256 and BLAKE3 under one prefixed format, and mandates SHA-256.** Grammar: `digest ::= algorithm ":" encoded`, `algorithm-component ::= [a-z0-9]+`, `encoded ::= [a-zA-Z0-9=_-]+`. Registered algorithm IDs: `sha256`, `sha512`, `blake3`. "Compliant implementations SHOULD use SHA-256" and "Implementations MUST implement SHA-256 digest verification for use in descriptors"; sha256 encoding is `/[a-f0-9]{64}/`. Implementations "SHOULD allow digests with unrecognized algorithms to pass validation if they comply with the above grammar." **This settles proposal 14: the prefix is not decoration, it is what lets one field carry both algorithms.**

14. **Wisp's own docs currently contradict themselves on the hash algorithm.** `docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md:58` says `blake3` with the rule "Hash raw persisted bytes when a contract requires a content hash", but the receipt example at line 163 is `"content_hash": "sha256:..."`, and `plan@1.spec_hash` in the shared schema specifies "Content hash (e.g. `sha256:<hex>`) of the spec@1 file". The schema is already shipped and consumed by `smith:recon`, so sha256 is the de-facto interchange hash and line 58 is the outlier.

15. **The constitution already answers Q-002's core rule, twice, and Wisp's own doc already lists the four receipt states.** Constitution: "IF the spec is written to disk but not committed to version control, it SHALL be treated as not yet persisted — an uncommitted file is invisible to a fresh checkout, a future session, and drift-checker", and the same for plans. `docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md:169-170`: "The operation must distinguish `validated`, `written_uncommitted`, `persisted`, and `commit_failed`. It cannot claim `persisted` when Git commit failed." Q-002's remaining live questions are therefore only: policy-file enforcement, and the no-Git-approval degradation path.

16. **Idempotent-write tooling universally distinguishes no-op from applied, and Wisp's Milestone 1 gate implicitly requires the same.** kubectl reports `unchanged` when "the maintained configuration has not changed" versus `configured` when "kubectl submitted an update"; Ansible reports `ok` ("the desired state was already present or no change was needed") versus `changed`. Milestone 1's gate says "Re-running the same persistence request is idempotent **or** reports an exact, typed conflict" — with only the four states above, the idempotent branch is indistinguishable from a fresh write.

17. **Tools that write files without committing treat that as a first-class mode, and at least one does it badly enough to be a cautionary tale.** cargo-release's dry-run "actually still makes changes to your working directory" — files modified, no commit, no tag — reported as issue #872 precisely because it "does a local commit with no feedback even in dry-run mode". Changesets makes committing opt-in config: "If you set the commit option in the config, the command will add the updated changeset files and then commit them" — i.e. write-only is the default and commit is the explicit escalation.

18. **Callisto encodes the write/no-write boundary in the type system rather than a boolean, via a zero-sized capability token.** `pub struct ApplyPermit { _private: () }` with "the one sanctioned construction path: mints a permit unless a dry run was requested. `dry_run` should come straight from the parsed CLI flag, read exactly once near the top of a command handler. Recomputing or re-deriving it deeper in a call stack reintroduces the divergence this type exists to eliminate." Every ref-writing method takes `permit: &ApplyPermit`, so "a dry run has none to give and therefore cannot call this at all."

19. **Identity-to-path has two opposed conventions in the field, and OpenSpec demonstrates the failure mode of the one Wisp did not pick.** OpenSpec derives identity from path — the hierarchical-structure proposal changes "the capability identifier from directory name to full relative path from `specs/`" — and its `openspec archive <change-id>` moves a change folder into `changes/archive/`, i.e. a routine lifecycle operation relocates the artifact and thereby changes its identity. Wisp's constitution takes the opposite convention: `<workspace_root>/docs/specs/<id>.json` and `docs/projects/<linked_spec>.json`, path derived from ID. Note that `plan@1`'s path is keyed by *another artifact's* id, so two plans for one spec collide by construction.

20. **`x-` prefixed keywords are the forward-compatible way to declare links in a JSON Schema today.** They "are compatible with all versions of JSON Schema that are currently published; they'll still just be collected as annotations", so a validator that does not know them ignores them rather than failing. The formal route is a custom vocabulary declared in a dialect metaschema ("a database schema dialect might add keywords like `indexed` or `foreignKey`"), which buys enforcement but costs a metaschema and a custom validator. JSON Hyper-Schema's `links`/`rel`/`targetSchema` was the standardized answer but the 2020-12 hypermedia document 404s on json-schema.org and the vocabulary is effectively dormant — do not build on it.

## Answers to the four questions asked

### (a) Typed `Freshness` for Q-010

The evidence says model this **per link, not per artifact** (finding 7: Tessl's ownership check is a spec→targets relation; finding 1: PROJECTMEM's rule is a decision→cited-file relation), and keep **two axes separate** (finding 2).

```rust
/// Did the artifact's own bytes change since a consumer recorded them?
/// Answerable with no Git at all — this is `plan@1.spec_hash` generalized.
pub enum ArtifactFreshness {
    Matches { hash: ContentHash },
    Diverged { recorded: ContentHash, current: ContentHash },
    Missing { expected_path: Utf8PathBuf },
}

/// Has the code this artifact-link points at moved on since the artifact was committed?
pub enum EvidenceFreshness {
    /// Worktree clean, HEAD == the commit that introduced the artifact.
    CleanAtCommit { commit: CommitSha },
    /// Worktree clean, HEAD has advanced but no commit touched the declared paths.
    CleanUnaffected { artifact_commit: CommitSha, head: CommitSha, commits_ahead: u32 },
    /// Worktree clean, N commits since the artifact touched declared paths.
    CleanBehind { artifact_commit: CommitSha, head: CommitSha, commits_touching: u32, touched_paths: Vec<Utf8PathBuf> },
    /// Worktree dirty, but no dirty path intersects the declared paths.
    DirtyUnaffected { head: CommitSha, dirty_path_count: usize },
    /// Worktree dirty and dirty paths intersect the declared paths.
    DirtyAffected { head: CommitSha, dirty_paths: Vec<Utf8PathBuf>, commits_touching: u32 },
    /// The artifact exists on disk but is not in any commit — commit distance is undefined.
    Uncommitted { path: Utf8PathBuf },
    /// No repository, shallow clone, or unresolvable artifact commit.
    Indeterminate { reason: FreshnessGap },
}
```

Four refinements over the brief's four-state list, each earned by a source:

- **`CleanBehind` carries `commits_touching`, not `commits_ahead`.** PROJECTMEM's message is "predates 7 commits **to auth.py**" — the count is filtered by path, which is what makes it actionable. An unfiltered distance-from-HEAD is noise in an active repo. Callisto's `commits_since_with_pathspec` computes exactly the filtered count (findings 1, 11).
- **`CleanUnaffected` must exist separately from `CleanAtCommit`.** Milestone 2's gate — "Editing an unrelated file does not invalidate an unrelated briefing" — is only expressible if "HEAD moved but not under my paths" is its own state.
- **`Uncommitted` is required, and it is the join point with Q-002.** An artifact in the `written_uncommitted` receipt state has no commit to measure distance from, so every other variant is a type error for it. Without this variant the implementation will silently fall back to `CleanAtCommit` and report a never-committed spec as current — precisely the failure the constitution's "an uncommitted file is invisible to a fresh checkout" rule exists to prevent (finding 15).
- **`Indeterminate` is required** because gix `rev_walk` errors, shallow clones, and detached/unborn HEAD are all reachable, and Wisp's provenance discipline forbids reporting an unknown as `Clean`.

Deliberately **not** in the enum: any `Stale` boolean or threshold constant. No source uses a threshold (finding 1: any N ≥ 1 flags), and the stale/fresh judgment is the briefing profile's policy over this data, not a property of the data. Keep the enum descriptive and let `brief` decide what warns.

Cost, per finding 11-12: one `Repository::status()` per workspace for the dirty-path set, and **one** `rev_walk` per distinct `since` commit with the **union** of all links' pathspecs, bucketed per link afterwards — not one walk per link. That is the concrete refinement to proposal 15.

### (b) Persist receipt states for Q-002

Keep `validated` / `written_uncommitted` / `persisted` / `commit_failed`, and add:

- **`already_current`** — candidate's canonical bytes equal the bytes already at the destination, and that file is committed. Directly demanded by Milestone 1's "idempotent or reports an exact, typed conflict" gate and by universal precedent (finding 16: kubectl `unchanged`, Ansible `ok`). **This forces a pipeline reordering**: `docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md:142-153` computes the content hash *after* the atomic write, so by the time the hash exists the evidence of a no-op has been overwritten. Canonicalize and hash the candidate *before* the temp-write, compare against the destination, and short-circuit.
- **`commit_declined { reason }`** — distinct from `commit_failed`. Q-002 asks for "how a harness with no Git write approval performs graceful degradation"; a refused approval is not an error and must not be reported as one, but per finding 5 it must be recorded rather than omitted. Reasons: `NotRequested`, `ApprovalDenied`, `NotARepository`, `PolicyDisabled`.
- **`conflict { existing_id, existing_path }`** — the other half of the Milestone 1 gate, and the enforcement point for Q-006 (see (e) below).

`superseded` is *not* a receipt state — it is a lifecycle status on the artifact (findings 3, 8). Do not fold the two.

One structural recommendation from finding 18: gate the commit behind an `ApplyPermit`-style zero-sized token minted once from the CLI flag plus harness approval, rather than threading a `bool commit` parameter. It makes `persisted`-without-a-commit unrepresentable instead of merely tested for, which is what the invariant "a receipt must never call an uncommitted file durable cross-session persistence" actually asks for.

### (c) Schema extension keyword for proposal 17

Use `x-wisp-link` as an annotation keyword now (finding 20: `x-` values are collected as annotations by every published JSON Schema version, so external validators and the direct-artifact fallback in `docs/02:172-178` keep working untouched). Defer a formal vocabulary + dialect metaschema until there is a second consumer.

```json
"linked_spec": {
  "type": "string",
  "description": "ID of the spec@1 this plan implements",
  "x-wisp-link": { "target_type": "spec@1", "by": "id", "cardinality": "one", "resolution": "required" }
},
"spec_file_path": {
  "type": "string",
  "x-wisp-link": { "target_type": "spec@1", "by": "path", "cardinality": "one", "resolution": "required", "same_target_as": "linked_spec" }
},
"spec_hash": {
  "type": "string",
  "x-wisp-hash-of": { "link": "linked_spec", "algorithms": ["sha256"] }
}
```

Two things this buys that nobody proposed. First, `same_target_as` makes the `linked_spec`/`spec_file_path` pair checkable — today nothing verifies that the id and the path name the same spec. Second, `x-wisp-hash-of` turns the constitution's Spec Staleness Detection rule from a plan→spec special case into a generic one: any field declared as the hash of a link becomes an `ArtifactFreshness` check for free, so `arch-model@1` or a future `brief` artifact inherits drift detection without new Rust. Backstage is the precedent that a generic processor over typed schema fields is sufficient (finding 9).

Also declare paths in the schema rather than in Rust, which is what Q-006 needs (see (e)):

```json
"$id": "plan@1",
"x-wisp-artifact": { "id_field": "linked_spec", "path_template": "docs/projects/{linked_spec}.json" }
```

### (d) Is `sha256:`-prefixed SHA-256 the right interchange hash?

Yes, and finding 13 makes the case stronger than "portable": OCI's `algorithm ":" encoded` grammar registers `sha256`, `sha512`, **and `blake3`** as sibling algorithm IDs. So the prefix is not a label on a sha256 field — it is the mechanism that lets one `content_hash` field carry `blake3:…` for an internal cache key and `sha256:…` for an interchange value without a second field or a format break. Adopt the OCI grammar verbatim, require `sha256` for anything crossing a process boundary (`plan@1.spec_hash` already does, finding 14), and permit `blake3:` internally.

Two consequences. **Fix `docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md:58`** — it currently mandates blake3 for "raw persisted bytes when a contract requires a content hash", which contradicts both the receipt example six lines from the schema it implements and the already-shipped `plan@1.spec_hash` (finding 14). The rule should read: sha256 for canonical artifact hashes in receipts and artifact fields, blake3 for `.wisp/` cache keys. **And specify what is hashed**: the constitution already says "over the raw file bytes as read from disk — not a parsed or re-serialized form", so the receipt's `content_hash` must be raw destination bytes post-write, which is consistent with the pipeline at line 149 but must survive the `already_current` reordering in (b) — hash the canonical candidate bytes, and they are by construction the bytes that will be written.

### (e) Q-006 identity and path mapping

Keep ID as the authority with path derived (constitution's `docs/specs/<id>.json`), not OpenSpec's path-derived identity — finding 19 shows the latter breaks on the tool's own archive operation. Declare the mapping in schema (`x-wisp-artifact.path_template`, above) so there is literally one public path-resolution table and it is data.

Enforce bijection at write time in `artifact persist`: before the temp-write, if the destination exists, parse it and compare its id field; a mismatch returns `conflict { existing_id, existing_path }` rather than overwriting. This is the write-time enforcement Q-006 asks for and no surveyed tool implements. Note the specific hazard finding 19 identifies: `plan@1`'s path is keyed by `linked_spec`, so two plans for one spec are a guaranteed collision, and the constitution's amendment rule ("SHALL overwrite the existing file at the same plan_file_path") makes that intentional — so for `plan@1` the conflict check must compare `linked_spec`, and an equal `linked_spec` is an amendment (allowed overwrite), not a conflict.

## Verdict on proposed changes

**13 — Freshness as a typed value on commit distance: confirm, with refinement.** The only two systems in the survey that mechanically check artifact-vs-code currency both do it this way (PROJECTMEM's "predates 7 commits to auth.py", Tessl's `check-target-ownership.sh`), and no spec-driven tool does better. Refinements: split into two axes (`ArtifactFreshness` bytes-changed vs `EvidenceFreshness` code-moved) because PROJECTMEM's own paper and README show these are separate mechanisms; make the count path-filtered, not distance-from-HEAD; add `CleanUnaffected`, `Uncommitted`, and `Indeterminate` to the brief's four states; carry no threshold constant.

**14 — SHA-256 for canonical hashes, blake3 for cache keys: confirm, strengthened.** OCI registers both under one prefixed grammar and mandates sha256 for interchange, so the split is standard rather than a compromise. Concrete action beyond the proposal: `docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md:58` currently says the opposite and must be corrected — it contradicts the receipt example at line 163 and the shipped `plan@1.spec_hash`.

**17 — Link declarations in schema metadata, not hardcoded Rust: confirm.** Backstage derives all catalog relations from typed spec fields via a generic processor and explicitly forbids hand-declared edges; Tessl builds its spec→requirements→targets→tests manifest from frontmatter with a script. Refinement: use `x-wisp-link` annotations (works with every published JSON Schema draft, does not break the direct-artifact fallback) rather than a custom vocabulary or JSON Hyper-Schema, which is dormant. Extend the idea to `x-wisp-hash-of` and `x-wisp-artifact.path_template` so freshness checking and path resolution are also data.

**Q-002 — commit policy: refine.** The core rule is already decided (constitution, twice) and the four states are already in Wisp's doc. What is missing: `already_current` (Milestone 1's idempotency gate cannot be met without it), `commit_declined` distinct from `commit_failed` (the no-approval degradation path Q-002 explicitly asks about), and `conflict`. Precedent for the write-without-commit default is Changesets (commit is opt-in config) and cargo-release (dry-run writes files) — and cargo-release's issue #872 is the warning that write-without-commit must be *reported*, not silent.

**Q-006 — identity and path mapping: refine.** Keep ID→path (OpenSpec's inverse convention breaks under its own `archive` command). Move the table into schema metadata. Enforce at write time by parsing the existing destination's id and returning a typed `conflict`; special-case `plan@1` where equal `linked_spec` means amendment, not collision.

**Q-010 — freshness semantics for dirty worktrees: refine.** Answer is the `EvidenceFreshness` enum in (a). The brief's four cases are right but incomplete; `Uncommitted` in particular is load-bearing because it is where Q-002 and Q-010 meet, and omitting it makes a never-committed artifact report as current.

## Recommendations not on the list

1. **Reuse `callisto-vcs` directly rather than reimplementing the walk.** It is `MIT OR Apache-2.0` (only `callisto-graph` and the root LICENSE are AGPL), so Q-003's licensing concern does not apply to the one crate Wisp actually wants. `commits_since_with_pathspec` already handles the branchy-history correctness case that a naive two-walk-and-exclude implementation gets wrong, and its doc comment explains why. This is a week of subtle work already done and tested.

2. **Adopt the `ApplyPermit` pattern for the commit step.** Zero-sized token minted once from the flag, required by every mutating call. Q-002's minimum invariant ("a receipt must never call an uncommitted file durable cross-session persistence") is currently a test; this makes it a compile error.

3. **Record declined commits and suppressed warnings, and surface them.** PROJECTMEM logs its own snooze and prints "one dim line so silence is never mistaken for a clean check." Wisp's briefing should carry the same: a `commit_declined` artifact and a suppressed freshness warning must both appear in the briefing's gap list, or the bounded-context guarantee (D-008) leaks.

4. **Add `superseded_by` as a typed field on artifact schemas, not a status string.** MADR and log4brains both encode supersession inside the status string and log4brains' maintainers document the resulting brittleness. PROJECTMEM's `--supersedes <id>` argument is the better shape. Wisp has no supersession model at all today; the `spec_contradiction` → corrected-spec loop overwrites in place, which means the superseded version exists only in Git history and cannot be cited by a briefing.

5. **Instrument the walk budget.** Callisto keeps a `REVWALK_VISIT_COUNT` atomic. Wisp's briefing compiler should carry commits-visited in its truncation/provenance record, so "freshness cost" is measurable before it becomes the reason a briefing is slow.

6. **The `spec_hash` field generalizes to a `linked_hash` on every link.** Only `plan@1` carries a hash of its source today. Any artifact citing another by id should be able to pin the bytes it read, which is what makes finding 6's advantage over Spec Kit/Kiro durable rather than accidental.

## Contradictions and open questions

1. **PROJECTMEM's paper and README describe different mechanisms** (finding 2). The paper's text positions commit-divergence drift detection as a *competitor's* approach while the README ships it as a 0.1.4 feature. Most likely explanation: the paper describes the pre-action gate and the README describes gate + staleness as two features; the paper may predate 0.1.4. I could not resolve this from the sources — the paper HTML has no staleness-algorithm section at all. Neither source gives the actual implementation (no source file was read), so the exact definition of "commits to auth.py" — first-parent tree diff, rename-following, merge handling — is **unverified**. Callisto's implementation is the one whose semantics I can quote precisely.

2. **No threshold constant found anywhere.** PROJECTMEM flags at any N ≥ 1 as far as the README shows, but neither source states this explicitly. If Wisp wants a warn-threshold, there is no precedent to copy and it should be config, not a constant.

3. **Kiro's sync behavior is only lightly sourced.** `kiro.dev/docs/specs/concepts/` returned 404 and I relied on search snippets plus Martin Fowler's comparison. The claim "Kiro has no automatic staleness detection between requirements/design/tasks" is *likely*, not confirmed — though Fowler's article explicitly containing no mention of drift detection for any of the three tools is reasonable corroboration.

4. **Tessl's `check-target-ownership.sh` mechanism is described but not read.** "Prevents target files from changing without spec updates" — whether that is a git-diff comparison in CI, a commit-distance check, or a mtime check is unstated in the fetched summary. If it matters, the tile repo (`github.com/tesslio/spec-driven-development-tile`) has the scripts.

5. **Changesets' current commit semantics are unverified.** The page fetched is self-marked outdated and redirects to `changesets.dev/guide/cli`, which I did not fetch. The claim "commit is opt-in config" holds for the version documented there.

6. **Whether `blake3` is worth keeping at all is open.** If `.wisp/` cache keys are the only blake3 consumer and briefings are dominated by git and Monokl cost, a single sha256 everywhere removes a dependency and a class of "which hash is this field" bugs. No evidence either way on whether Wisp's hashing volume justifies two algorithms — that is a measurement, not a literature question.

1	# Wisp: Delivery Plan and Acceptance Gates
2	
3	## Delivery principle
4	
5	Build the durable, portable path before the convenient path.
6	
7	The first useful Wisp release is not a vector search UI or a daemon. It is a
8	reliable way to validate, persist, inspect, and join canonical artifacts with
9	Git and Monokl evidence. The MCP becomes valuable because it exposes that
10	working core; it must not be the reason the core exists.
11	
12	## Milestone 0 — contracts and fixtures
13	
14	### Deliverables
15	
16	- A pinned, immutable schema registry strategy for all initial artifact types.
17	- A Wisp configuration schema describing artifact locations and workspace
18	  discovery rules.
19	- Fixture workspaces covering valid, invalid, stale, missing, and
20	  cross-harness artifact chains.
21	- Public DTOs for artifact receipts, provenance, freshness, impact evidence,
22	  and briefings.
23	- A compatibility statement for direct-artifact fallback.
24	
25	### Required decisions
26	
27	- Where the canonical plugin schemas are published and how Wisp pins them.
28	- Whether Wisp itself is the owner of the schema registry or consumes a small,
29	  independently versioned `orin-contracts` package.
30	- Wisp's license and whether it permits reuse of any AGPL implementation code.
31	- Artifact commit policy: when an operation may create a commit and how an
32	  unavailable/declined commit is represented.
33	
34	### Acceptance gates
35	
36	- A fixture can validate every supported schema version without reaching into
37	  a mutable sibling checkout.
38	- Invalid properties, invalid IDs, and broken links fail with typed errors.
39	- A no-Wisp fixture can consume the same JSON artifacts directly.
40	
41	## Milestone 1 — library and artifact CLI
42	
43	### Deliverables
44	
45	- `wisp-model`, `wisp-schema`, and `wisp-artifacts`.
46	- `wisp artifact validate`, `get`, `list`, and `persist` CLI commands.
47	- Deterministic serialization and raw-byte content hashing.
48	- Temp-file/rename writes and an explicit commit receipt state.
49	- `wisp status` reporting artifact graph/freshness without code intelligence.
50	
51	### Acceptance gates
52	
53	- A failed validation leaves no canonical target file and no cache mutation.
54	- A successful write is atomic under interruption simulation.
55	- A persistence receipt distinguishes `written_uncommitted` from `persisted`.
56	- Re-running the same persistence request is idempotent or reports an exact,
57	  typed conflict; it never creates ambiguous duplicate artifacts.
58	- CLI JSON output is snapshot-tested and stable across supported platforms.
59	
60	## Milestone 2 — derived artifact graph and Git evidence
61	
62	### Deliverables
63	
64	- `wisp-git` with repository discovery, HEAD/tree/worktree fingerprints, and
65	  changed-file evidence using `gix`.
66	- `wisp-store` with SQLite migrations, artifact graph, link validation,
67	  freshness calculation, and FTS for selected tracked documents.
68	- `wisp impact` based on declared artifact files/links and Git file changes.
69	- Rebuild command: delete/recreate all `.wisp/` state from source of truth.
70	
71	### Acceptance gates
72	
73	- Deleting `.wisp/` then rebuilding produces the same derived graph from the
74	  same workspace snapshot.
75	- Editing a spec changes its hash and marks linked plans/briefs stale.
76	- Editing an unrelated file does not invalidate an unrelated briefing.
77	- A dirty worktree is represented distinctly from a clean commit snapshot.
78	- Concurrent read operations cannot observe partial SQLite state.
79	
80	## Milestone 3 — Monokl adapter and context compiler
81	
82	### Deliverables
83	
84	- `wisp-monokl` CLI adapter using Monokl's stable typed/JSON surface.
85	- `wisp-context` with `brief implement`, `brief review`, and `brief
86	  architecture-audit` profiles.
87	- Evidence provenance and Monokl precision carried into every code-backed
88	  briefing result.
89	- Brief cache keys and explicit truncation records.
90	
91	### Acceptance gates
92	
93	- A Smith-style implementation briefing retrieves the plan from disk, its
94	  linked spec, relevant criteria, declared files, relevant tests, applicable
95	  architecture constraints, and current Git delta.
96	- A stale spec hash makes the plan's freshness warning visible in the briefing.
97	- Unsupported/heuristic code analysis is labeled; Wisp never reports it as
98	  exact.
99	- Briefing output stays below a configured budget and lists what was omitted.
100	- Monokl unavailable/error produces a useful artifact-only briefing with a
101	  typed `code_evidence_unavailable` gap rather than a fabricated answer.
102	
103	## Milestone 4 — MCP surface and Michi output integration
104	
105	### Deliverables
106	
107	- MCP outcomes with complete typed structured content and a basic deterministic
108	  text renderer.
109	- A Michi-backed TOON/KV/hints adapter using the local sibling checkout during
110	  coordinated development.

112	  versioned release suitable for a non-path dependency.
113	- `wisp-mcp` tools/resources mapping one-to-one to library operations.
114	- Tool schemas, mutation safeguards, and clear recovery hints.

120	- Text/TOON output, when TOON is enabled, is derived from the same typed result
121	  and never reparsed.
122	- Read-only MCP calls cause no canonical file, Git, or cache-write side effect

126	
127	## Milestone 5 — service mode and cache optimization

129	### Deliverables

132	- Single-writer coordination for SQLite derived state.

146	
147	## Milestone 6 — optional semantic retrieval

161	  source-backed evidence.

# Wisp: Delivery Plan and Acceptance Gates

## Delivery principle

Build the durable, portable path before the convenient path.

The first useful Wisp release is not a vector search UI or a daemon. It is a
reliable way to validate, persist, inspect, and join canonical artifacts with
Git and Monokl evidence. The MCP becomes valuable because it exposes that
working core; it must not be the reason the core exists.

## Milestone 0 — contracts and fixtures

### Deliverables

- A pinned, immutable schema registry strategy for all initial artifact types.
- A Wisp configuration schema describing artifact locations and workspace
  discovery rules.
- Fixture workspaces covering valid, invalid, stale, missing, and
  cross-harness artifact chains.
- Public DTOs for artifact receipts, provenance, freshness, impact evidence,
  and briefings.
- A compatibility statement for direct-artifact fallback.

### Required decisions

- Where the canonical plugin schemas are published and how Wisp pins them.
- Whether Wisp itself is the owner of the schema registry or consumes a small,
  independently versioned `orin-contracts` package.
- Wisp's license and whether it permits reuse of any AGPL implementation code.
- Artifact commit policy: when an operation may create a commit and how an
  unavailable/declined commit is represented.

### Acceptance gates

- A fixture can validate every supported schema version without reaching into
  a mutable sibling checkout.
- Invalid properties, invalid IDs, and broken links fail with typed errors.
- A no-Wisp fixture can consume the same JSON artifacts directly.

## Milestone 1 — library and artifact CLI

### Deliverables

- `wisp-model`, `wisp-schema`, and `wisp-artifacts`.
- `wisp artifact validate`, `get`, `list`, and `persist` CLI commands.
- Deterministic serialization and raw-byte content hashing.
- Temp-file/rename writes and an explicit commit receipt state.
- `wisp status` reporting artifact graph/freshness without code intelligence.

### Acceptance gates

- A failed validation leaves no canonical target file and no cache mutation.
- A successful write is atomic under interruption simulation.
- A persistence receipt distinguishes `written_uncommitted` from `persisted`.
- Re-running the same persistence request is idempotent or reports an exact,
  typed conflict; it never creates ambiguous duplicate artifacts.
- CLI JSON output is snapshot-tested and stable across supported platforms.

## Milestone 2 — derived artifact graph and Git evidence

### Deliverables

- `wisp-git` with repository discovery, HEAD/tree/worktree fingerprints, and
  changed-file evidence using `gix`.
- `wisp-store` with SQLite migrations, artifact graph, link validation,
  freshness calculation, and FTS for selected tracked documents.
- `wisp impact` based on declared artifact files/links and Git file changes.
- Rebuild command: delete/recreate all `.wisp/` state from source of truth.

### Acceptance gates

- Deleting `.wisp/` then rebuilding produces the same derived graph from the
  same workspace snapshot.
- Editing a spec changes its hash and marks linked plans/briefs stale.
- Editing an unrelated file does not invalidate an unrelated briefing.
- A dirty worktree is represented distinctly from a clean commit snapshot.
- Concurrent read operations cannot observe partial SQLite state.

## Milestone 3 — Monokl adapter and context compiler

### Deliverables

- `wisp-monokl` CLI adapter using Monokl's stable typed/JSON surface.
- `wisp-context` with `brief implement`, `brief review`, and `brief
  architecture-audit` profiles.
- Evidence provenance and Monokl precision carried into every code-backed
  briefing result.
- Brief cache keys and explicit truncation records.

### Acceptance gates

- A Smith-style implementation briefing retrieves the plan from disk, its
  linked spec, relevant criteria, declared files, relevant tests, applicable
  architecture constraints, and current Git delta.
- A stale spec hash makes the plan's freshness warning visible in the briefing.
- Unsupported/heuristic code analysis is labeled; Wisp never reports it as
  exact.
- Briefing output stays below a configured budget and lists what was omitted.
- Monokl unavailable/error produces a useful artifact-only briefing with a
  typed `code_evidence_unavailable` gap rather than a fabricated answer.

## Milestone 4 — MCP surface and Michi output integration

### Deliverables

- MCP outcomes with complete typed structured content and a basic deterministic
  text renderer.
- A Michi-backed TOON/KV/hints adapter using the local sibling checkout during
  coordinated development.
- A release gate: Wisp is not published until Michi has a compatible,
  versioned release suitable for a non-path dependency.
- `wisp-mcp` tools/resources mapping one-to-one to library operations.
- Tool schemas, mutation safeguards, and clear recovery hints.
- Harness adapter examples for Claude, Codex, and a direct CLI fallback.

### Acceptance gates

- Every MCP tool's `structuredContent` is equivalent to the CLI JSON result.
- Text/TOON output, when TOON is enabled, is derived from the same typed result
  and never reparsed.
- Read-only MCP calls cause no canonical file, Git, or cache-write side effect
  beyond explicitly documented harmless read/access metadata.
- A harness without MCP can run the matching CLI operation and obtain the same
  semantic result.

## Milestone 5 — service mode and cache optimization

### Deliverables

- Optional `wisp-service`/`wispd` workspace-scoped process.
- Single-writer coordination for SQLite derived state.
- Filesystem/Git invalidation watcher.
- Warm Monokl session integration once Monokl offers a stable library/session
  API.
- Service health, version/config compatibility, and graceful cold fallback.

### Acceptance gates

- Two CLI/MCP clients can query the same workspace concurrently without cache
  corruption or cross-request evidence leakage.
- A source/artifact change invalidates precisely the dependent records.
- Stopping the service leaves the CLI able to perform a correct cold query.
- Service response correctness equals one-shot library response correctness for
  the same fixed workspace snapshot.

## Milestone 6 — optional semantic retrieval

### Deliverables

- An opt-in `wisp-semantic` feature, provider/configuration boundary, and
  content-hash/versioned embedding records.
- Candidate retrieval for prose documents and decisions.
- Verification pass from candidate to current canonical source.

### Acceptance gates

- Wisp works fully when semantic retrieval is disabled.
- A deleted or modified source invalidates its vector chunks immediately.
- Every semantic result identifies whether it is merely a candidate or verified
  source-backed evidence.
- Privacy/network policy is explicit; no document is sent to a provider by
  default.

## Cross-harness scenarios

The fixture suite must test the actual value proposition, not only unit types.

| Scenario | Expected durable chain |
| --- | --- |
| Claude specification → Codex planning | `spec@1` written/committed, Codex reads it from its path and writes `plan@1` |
| Codex planning → Claude implementation | Claude reads the persisted plan and source spec, not an old conversation copy |
| Architecture audit before planning | model is missing → built once → later harness checks it and emits an audit |
| Spec contradiction | implementation emits contradiction → corrected spec replaces same path → amended plan replaces same path |
| No Wisp installation | Direct JSON/schema route preserves baseline behavior and reports only lost enrichment |
| Monokl unavailable | Artifact/Git briefing continues, code-evidence gap is explicit |
| Dirty worktree | Brief identifies changed files and states whether plan/spec evidence predates them |

## Evaluation plan

Use Prism to compare paired runs on a frozen task suite:

1. baseline: plugin receives direct artifact/filesystem context only;
2. treatment: same plugin receives the corresponding Wisp briefing.

Record task pass rate, evidence completeness, criterion coverage, incorrect
stale assumptions, total tokens, cache read/write tokens where available,
latency, tool calls, and cost. Use Lumen to inspect actual trajectories and
detect retrieval/tool cycles. Wisp should not claim value based only on smaller
payloads; a smaller briefing is an improvement only if the task result remains
as correct and complete.

## Non-goals for the first release

- native named-agent packaging for every harness;
- arbitrary chat-history memory;
- mandatory daemon/service installation;
- embeddings/vector search;
- copying Monokl's AST/index into Wisp;
- remote multi-user synchronization;
- autonomous commit/push/PR creation;
- a generalized DAG agent-workflow engine.

1	# Wisp: Architecture and Contracts
2	
3	## System view
4	
5	```text
6	                         canonical inputs
7	 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
8	 │ Git worktree/history   docs/*.json   ADRs/docs   Monokl evidence   │
9	 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
10	              │                 │              │              │
11	              └─────────────────┴──────┬───────┴──────────────┘
12	                                       ▼
13	                         wisp-workspace / wisp-context
14	                         validate · join · rank · bound · cite
15	                                       │
16	                   ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
17	                   ▼                                       ▼
18	            rebuildable `.wisp/`                    typed result model
19	            SQLite / FTS / brief cache                       │
20	                                                           ┌─┴──────────────┐
21	                                                           ▼                ▼
22	                                                    wisp CLI          wisp MCP
23	                                                    JSON/TOON          MCP result
24	```
25	
26	The library owns the behavior. The CLI and MCP must not reimplement artifact
27	validation, cache invalidation, Git inspection, ranking, or response shaping.
28	
29	## Proposed workspace crates
30	
31	| Crate | Responsibility | Dependency direction |
32	| --- | --- | --- |
33	| `wisp-model` | Public IDs, DTOs, provenance, freshness, query/result contracts | Depends on no Wisp crate |
34	| `wisp-schema` | Schema registry, validation, immutable schema-version resolution | `wisp-model` |
35	| `wisp-artifacts` | Configured paths, parsing, deterministic serialization, atomic writes, artifact-link validation | model, schema |
36	| `wisp-git` | Repository discovery, snapshots, diff and commit evidence | model; `gix` or compatible adapter |
37	| `wisp-monokl` | Typed adapter over Monokl queries and precision metadata | model; Monokl public API |
38	| `wisp-store` | SQLite/FTS schema, derived relationship graph, cache/invalidation metadata | model |
39	| `wisp-context` | Context and impact compiler; source selection, evidence reduction, freshness decisions | artifacts, git, monokl, store |
40	| `wisp-output` | Optional TOON/KV/hints/MCP presentation conversion using local Michi during development | model/context; Michi |
41	| `wisp-service` | Optional workspace-scoped long-lived process, watcher, request coordination | context/output/store |
42	| `wisp-cli` | Clap/CLI boundary, JSON input/output, human diagnostics | service or context/output |
43	| `wisp-mcp` | MCP transport, tools/resources mapped directly to service/library calls | service/output |
44	| `wisp-fixtures` | Fixture workspaces, contract fixtures, integration/evaluation helpers | test-only |
45	
46	`wisp-model` is deliberately boring and stable. It must not depend on Tokio,
47	MCP transport types, Monokl implementation types, SQLite, or CLI formatting.
48	
49	## Recommended implementation crates
50	
51	| Concern | Recommendation | Rule |
52	| --- | --- | --- |
53	| JSON | `serde`, `serde_json` | Canonical artifact schemas remain separately versioned contracts |
54	| Schema | `schemars` plus a JSON Schema validator | Generated Rust schema is helpful; the pinned JSON schema is authoritative |
55	| Errors | `thiserror` | Domain crates expose typed errors, never CLI strings |
56	| CLI diagnostics | `miette` | CLI boundary only; never the MCP data contract |
57	| Paths | `camino` | Workspace-facing paths use UTF-8 path types consistently |
58	| Hashes | `blake3` | Hash raw persisted bytes when a contract requires a content hash |
59	| Atomic I/O | `tempfile`, `fs2` | Temp-write/rename and inter-process writer coordination |
60	| Git | `gix` | Use typed/in-process Git operations; preserve exact commit/tree IDs |
61	| Relational/FTS | `rusqlite` + SQLite FTS5 | Local-first, synchronous core, single-writer aware |
62	| CPU work | `rayon` | Independent CPU-bound collection/reduction only |
63	| Service I/O | `tokio` | Optional service/MCP/watch boundary; do not leak into models |
64	| Tracing | `tracing` | Structured operational events; no raw sensitive content by default |
65	| Filesystem watch | `notify` | Service phase only, never required for correctness |
66	| Snapshot/property tests | `insta`, `proptest` | Verify deterministic render and graph/invalidation invariants |
67	
68	Avoid an async database abstraction until Wisp becomes a real networked service.
69	Avoid a persistent code-search engine because Monokl already owns code search.
70	Avoid a vector dependency in the initial build.
71	
72	## Monokl integration
73	
74	### Ownership boundary
75	
76	Monokl owns current code facts:
77	
78	- parsing and per-language analyzer capability;
79	- symbols, definitions, references, imports, exports, blocks, and code search;
80	- the content-hash-backed parse cache and code-workspace index;
81	- precision level and provenance of each code result.
82	
83	Wisp owns cross-domain relevance:
84	
85	- mapping an artifact task to relevant files/symbols/tests;
86	- mapping a Git delta to likely affected artifacts/invariants;
87	- enforcing artifact links, hashes, and freshness;
88	- compiling a bounded briefing with provenance.
89	
90	Wisp must not copy Monokl's AST data into SQLite as a rival code index. It may
91	store stable pointers to a Monokl result—workspace fingerprint, code content
92	hash, symbol identity/path/range, operation, precision, and query parameters—
93	when doing so accelerates a derived impact or briefing query.
94	
95	### Integration phases
96	
97	1. **CLI adapter:** invoke Monokl's stable JSON/agent output interface; cache
98	   no opaque Monokl internals in Wisp.
99	2. **Library adapter:** once Monokl publishes a stable public Rust API, embed
100	   it in `wisp-monokl` and exchange typed records directly.
101	3. **Shared workspace service:** a Wisp service can own one Monokl workspace
102	   session, keeping Monokl's in-memory parse/cache and workspace index warm.
103	
104	At all phases, Monokl remains responsible for invalidating code facts on source
105	content changes. Wisp invalidates only its derived records that depend on those
106	facts.
107	
108	### Precision is carried through
109	
110	Every code-backed Wisp claim includes Monokl's capability/precision and
111	provenance. For example, an impact edge based on an exact TypeScript resolver
112	is materially different from one derived from a structural Rust module-path
113	walk or a heuristic fallback. Wisp must never silently upgrade the confidence
114	of a code relationship.
115	
116	## Artifact model and persistence
117	
118	### Canonical artifacts
119	
120	The initial target contracts are the plugin ecosystem's versioned JSON schemas:
121	
122	- `requirement@1`
123	- `research-report@1`
124	- `spec@1`
125	- `plan@1`
126	- `arch-model@1`
127	- `arch-audit@1`
128	- `verdict@1`/`verdict@2`
129	- `finding-report@1`
130	- `changeset@2` and `release-artifact@2` where relevant
131	
132	Schemas must be immutable by version. Wisp needs a pinned schema registry: a
133	published `orin-contracts` package or a vendored, checksummed schema bundle is
134	an explicit prerequisite. It must not silently read a mutable schema file from
135	an unrelated checkout and call it `@1`.
136	
137	### Persist operation
138	
139	An artifact producer creates a candidate JSON document. Wisp then performs the
140	durable mechanics:
141	
142	```text
143	candidate JSON
144	  → resolve schema version
145	  → validate shape and artifact links
146	  → derive canonical destination from artifact type/ID
147	  → deterministic serialization
148	  → atomic temp write + rename
149	  → read raw bytes and compute content hash
150	  → commit if the selected workflow requires it
151	  → invalidate/rebuild affected Wisp derived records
152	  → return typed persistence receipt
153	```
154	
155	Example receipt:
156	
157	```json
158	{
159	  "status": "persisted",
160	  "artifact_type": "spec@1",
161	  "id": "SPEC-021",
162	  "path": "docs/specs/SPEC-021.json",
163	  "content_hash": "sha256:...",
164	  "source_revision": "git:abc123",
165	  "cache_invalidated": ["brief:smith:PLAN-014"]
166	}
167	```
168	
169	The operation must distinguish `validated`, `written_uncommitted`, `persisted`,
170	and `commit_failed`. It cannot claim `persisted` when Git commit failed.
171	
172	### Direct-artifact fallback
173	
174	Wisp is preferred but optional. Plugins retain documented direct JSON behavior:
175	they can read a path from `spec_file_path`/`plan_file_path`, validate against a
176	bundled schema, and record a capability/freshness gap if Wisp is not available.
177	This preserves cross-harness interoperability and allows adoption one workspace
178	at a time.
179	
180	## Cache and store design
181	
182	### Directory layout
183	
184	```text
185	.wisp/
186	  config.toml                 # optional local configuration; tracked only by choice
187	  state.sqlite                # derived artifact/relation/FTS state
188	  cache/
189	    briefs/                   # bounded compiled context packets
190	    queries/                  # optional materialized query results
191	  locks/                      # workspace service/writer coordination
192	  diagnostics/                # optional sanitized operational diagnostics
193	```
194	
195	Everything in `.wisp/` is rebuildable. Canonical artifacts remain outside it.
196	
197	### SQLite tables, conceptually
198	
199	| Table/view | Contents | Invalidation key |
200	| --- | --- | --- |
201	| `artifacts` | ID, type/version, canonical path, raw hash, source Git state | artifact raw bytes + config |
202	| `artifact_edges` | implements, links_to, governed_by, supersedes relationships | endpoint hashes |
203	| `source_snapshots` | resolved HEAD/tree/worktree fingerprint | Git state |
204	| `code_evidence_refs` | pointers to Monokl operations/results, not copied ASTs | source hash + Monokl config/version |
205	| `impact_edges` | derived artifact ↔ module/file/symbol relationships with evidence | inputs above |
206	| `briefs` | cache key, bounded payload, source pointers, truncation record | every input hash + request |
207	| FTS virtual tables | selected docs/artifacts and metadata | document raw hash + tokenizer config |
208	
209	### Cache keys
210	
211	A briefing key includes at least:
212	
213	```text
214	workspace canonical root
215	+ Wisp configuration hash
216	+ source snapshot (HEAD/tree plus dirty-worktree fingerprint)
217	+ each artifact's raw-byte hash
218	+ Monokl version/config/query identity
219	+ requested stage, selected task, detail/budget options
220	```
221	
222	When one element changes, Wisp must discard or recompute the dependent result.
223	It must not use filesystem modification time as the authoritative identity of a
224	canonical artifact or source file.
225	
226	### Multi-process safety
227	
228	SQLite allows many readers but only one writer. The preferred daemon mode is
229	one workspace-scoped Wisp service owning write coordination and a warm Monokl
230	session. CLI clients may attach to it or run one-shot read-only/rebuild work.
231	
232	If multiple Wisp processes are allowed to write, they need an explicit
233	inter-process lock and transaction/retry contract. A Rust `Mutex` alone is not
234	enough. Likewise, Wisp must not directly write Monokl's cache; it asks Monokl
235	to manage its own cache lifecycle.
236	
237	## Semantic retrieval and vectors
238	
239	SQLite FTS is the first document retrieval mechanism. An optional later
240	`wisp-semantic` capability may add embeddings for prose queries such as
241	"where did we decide tenant isolation rules?".
242	
243	Vector rows must carry:
244	
245	- the source artifact/document ID and path;
246	- the exact source content hash and chunk bounds;
247	- embedding model/provider/chunking version;
248	- an opt-in privacy configuration.
249	
250	Vector retrieval returns `candidates`. Wisp then reads the current canonical
251	source and reports it as evidence or rejects it as stale. It must never answer
252	"the architecture says X" solely because a vector nearest-neighbor result did.
253	
254	No embeddings are needed for code retrieval: Monokl's lexical and structural
255	signals are the primary code path.
256	
257	## Context compiler
258	
259	### Briefing contract
260	
261	`wisp-context` produces a typed `Briefing` with these conceptual sections:
262	
263	| Section | Contents |
264	| --- | --- |
265	| Request | stage, goal, workspace snapshot, requested task/detail budget |
266	| Governing artifacts | spec/plan/requirement/decision pointers and verified hashes |
267	| Criteria | only acceptance criteria relevant to the requested task |
268	| Architecture | applicable invariants, canonical abstractions, boundary rules |
269	| Code evidence | Monokl symbols, definitions, references, tests, precision/provenance |
270	| Git evidence | current changes, relevant commits/diff scope, staleness warnings |
271	| Risks/gaps | absent artifact, stale plan, missing model coverage, unsupported language |
272	| Next actions | bounded, deterministic follow-up queries—not autonomous instructions |
273	| Truncation | omitted categories/counts and exact retrieval expansion path |
274	
275	### Briefing selection policy
276	
277	1. Include required governing artifacts before optional supporting context.
278	2. Prefer exact, current evidence over broad or low-precision evidence.
279	3. Select files/symbols by explicit artifact link, task file declaration,
280	   Monokl impact evidence, and Git delta—not semantic similarity alone.
281	4. Include tests that prove selected criteria before unrelated test inventory.
282	5. Enforce a budget and expose truncation; do not silently omit evidence.
283	6. Never include raw chain-of-thought or private session content in a briefing.
284	
285	## CLI contract
286	
287	The CLI is the first stable integration surface. Every automation-capable
288	command supports `--format json`; text/TOON are presentation modes.
289	
290	Illustrative commands:
291	
292	```bash
293	wisp artifact validate --input candidate.json --type spec@1 --format json
294	wisp artifact persist --input candidate.json --type spec@1 --commit --format json
295	wisp artifact get SPEC-021 --format json
296	wisp status --workspace . --format json
297	wisp brief implement --plan PLAN-014 --task T2 --format json
298	wisp impact --paths src/retry/policy.rs --format json
299	wisp verify workflow --scenario claude-spec_codex-plan --format json
300	```
301	
302	CLI JSON must be deterministic enough for snapshot/fixture tests. Human output
303	uses `miette` diagnostics and, where appropriate, Michi rendering only after
304	the typed operation completes.
305	
306	## MCP contract
307	
308	MCP follows the CLI/library contract rather than inventing another API.
309	
310	Initial tools:
311	
312	| MCP tool | Maps to | Mutation |
313	| --- | --- | --- |
314	| `wisp_artifact_get` | artifact read/validation | no |
315	| `wisp_artifact_persist` | artifact persist | yes; explicit |
316	| `wisp_brief` | context compiler | no |
317	| `wisp_impact` | impact query | no |
318	| `wisp_status` | workflow/freshness status | no |
319	| `wisp_verify` | fixture/contract verification | no |
320	
321	Initial resources may expose read-only canonical artifact URIs, e.g.
322	`wisp://workspace/<id>/artifact/SPEC-021` and a current status resource. The
323	MCP result should contain both:
324	
325	- compact agent-facing content (TOON/KV/hints through Michi where appropriate);
326	  and
327	- complete typed `structuredContent` matching the library result.
328	
329	TOON is appropriate for uniform candidate lists such as symbols, files,
330	criteria, findings, and affected artifacts. It is not a replacement for a
331	canonical JSON artifact or a mutation payload.
